 Learn more Uber ( UBER ) is scheduled to report third quarter results on Wednesday. Investors expect the ride-hailing giant to post bookings above the midpoint of its guidance and keep adding users at a double-digit clip. 
 Uber is expected to post gross bookings of $59.8 billion per Bloomberg consensus, up 20% year over year. That's above the $59.25 billion midpoint of Uber's guidance range of $58.25 billion to $60.25 billion. Gross bookings measure the total dollar value of rides and orders, such as Uber Eats deliveries, on the platform. 
 Investors will also watch monthly active platform consumers (MAPCs), the number of unique users who take a ride or place an order each month. Analysts see 215 million MAPCs, up 14% from 189 million a year ago. Uber posted 208 million in the second quarter, up 16%. 
 Uber stock fell 0.3% during premarket trading on Wednesday. 
 ( UBER )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 66.60 -0.11 (-0.16%) At close: November 3 at 4:00:03 PM EST 66.75 +0.14 (+0.21%) Pre-Market: 7:12:33 AM EST In terms of overall figures, revenue is expected to come in at $14.65 billion, up 9% year over year. Uber is expected to post adjusted EPS of $0.87, within the company's guidance of $0.84 to $0.88. 
 Adjusted EBITDA is expected at $2.93 billion vs. $2.26 billion a year ago. That's up 30% and in the upper half of Uber's $2.86 billion to $2.96 billion outlook. 
 Uber investors are looking for a strong quarter. Uber shares are down almost 30% over the past year. 
 Uber spent heavily on deals this year. It agreed to buy corporate catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in October and launched a $14.8 billion takeover offer for Delivery Hero in July. Meanwhile, rival DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for $17 billion last week. 
 Lucid Gravity robotaxi with next-gen sensor array featuring high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar sensors, and radars that provides 360-degree perception, as well as a purpose-built roof-mounted halo designed to maximize sensor visibility. (Courtesy of Uber) · Uber Then there's Uber's robotaxi efforts. Investors will look for an update on CEO Dara Khosrowshahi's target of robotaxis in as many as 15 cities by year-end. They'll also want to know how Uber fills the gap left by Waymo, which is unwinding its partnership with the company. 
 Uber is working with Lucid ( LCID ) and Rivian ( RIVN ) to build its own robotaxi networks, and has said it will commit more than $10 billion to such partnerships. 
 TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge sees Wednesday's report as a possible catalyst for the stock. 
 "We see potential for share upside as our outlook for Uber remains strong, given i) '26 Mobility GB reported growth in the high teens y/y (x-FX), supported by accelerating US biz led by CA insurance relief, geo expansion, and fast-paced growth from emerging products including Uber for Business, Reserve, Shuttle," he wrote in a note in late October. 
 Blackledge rates Uber a Buy with a $118 price target.
